correctness.rationale: Binary projection identity P_A=E+u_A⊗ℓ_A/[a(1−a)] is checked on both atoms. E annihilates centered rank-one factors, and each adjacent composition inserts covariance d_i, giving W−E=c um⊗ℓ1. Sharp Hölder duality yields ||W−E||_p=|c|h_p(am)h_q(a1); its rank-one square equals θ times itself, yielding all positive powers even θ=0. Reversing factors flips endpoint p/q norms; at p=2 those coincide for every event pair. For a rare atom ε nested inside B of measure 1/2, ratio behaves ε^(2/p−1), unbounded on one orientation whenever p≠2. Independently verified 4-equiprobable-atom events A1={2,3}, A2={1,2,3}, A3={1,3}: adjacent covariances 1/8 while endpoint covariance 0, giving W≠E but W²=E.
residual_risks: No claim that W^k converges to E when |θ|≥1; nonbinary sigma-algebras and p endpoints excluded.

value.rationale: Provides a sharp quantitative classification of the natural minimal two-cell subclass of Lp conditional-expectation products, including exact convergence rates, finite-step mixing without zero adjacent correlations, and a mathematically meaningful p=2 versus p≠2 time-reversal dichotomy on only three atoms. Not just a routine norm computation because the global order-comparison obstruction answers a structural Banach question.
residual_risks: Does not address nonbinary sigma-algebras, endpoints p=1/∞, or general contractions.

final_claim: Every real Lp 1<p<∞ ordered product of nondegenerate binary conditional expectations has centered rank-one form W−E=c um⊗ℓ1, exact all-iterate norms |θ|^(k−1)|c| h_p(am)h_q(a1), and reversal has universal equal norm precisely when p=2; for any p≠2 reversal norms are not uniformly comparable, already on three atoms.
